Subject: PHI retention & redaction options for procurement review

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — we liked the latency profile and the ability to pin models. Before procurement we need firm answers on a few regulated-data items so the procurement and security teams can sign off. Can you confirm the following for PHI (protected health information) workloads?

1) Default retention windows for request/response content and for operational logs in the hosted API. Are those configurable per-account?
2) What redaction options do you offer? We need both proactive (strip before storage) and retroactive (scrub existing stored records) approaches.
3) For Dedicated/Private deployments: how does data residency work (data plane in our VPC vs. Redwood managed storage) and who can trigger permanent deletion?
4) Auditability: can you provide tamper-evident proof of deletion and the SOC 2 report?
5) Legal holds / e-discovery: if a regulator issues a hold, how is that respected and what is the retention override process?

We're on a tight timeline — procurement would like to close next week. Attaching our internal security checklist separately (not included here).

Appreciate a concise runbook we can share with legal/security.

— Elena
Dr. Elena Soto
Director, Clinical IT
St. Mary's Health
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Elena Soto <elena.soto@st-marys-health.org>
Cc: Andrew Li <andrew.li@medtechsolutions.com>, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

Subject: Re: PHI retention & redaction options for procurement review

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Summary answers below; I kept it high-level and added practical next steps at the end. I'm attaching our retention matrix and the SOC 2 summary.

1) Hosted API defaults (standard offering):
   - Request/response content: default 30 days for troubleshooting & quality (configurable).
   - Operational logs/metadata (routes, latency, errors): retained 90 days by default.
   - Both of the above are configurable via account settings; we can enable an "ephemeral mode" that disables content logging entirely (no request/response stored).

2) Redaction options:
   - Proactive (recommended): client-side redaction + API-level redaction filters. We expose multiple strategies: 
     * pii_mask: replace detected PII/PHI spans with tokens (e.g., [REDACTED_NAME]).
     * pii_hash: reversible hashing bound to your KMS (useful for deduplication without revealing raw data).
     * full_redact: strip entire prompt/response contents prior to any persistent storage.
   - Retroactive (hosted): limited. If content was retained under the previous policy we can perform a service-side purge, but retroactive structural redaction (e.g., replace substrings inside an archived blob) is only guaranteed in Dedicated/Private where you control storage or have export access. For hosted, we provide deletion certs and proof of purge (see #4).
   - Caching / KV cache: we support per-customer KV cache scrubbing and ability to disable prefix caching for sessions that contain PHI.

3) Dedicated / Private:
   - Dedicated: data plane is in Redwood-managed infrastructure but logically isolated; retention policies are configurable per-tenant and Redwood support can execute deletions on request with purge timelines agreed in contract.
   - Private (VPC / on-prem): data remains in your environment; Redwood control plane metadata is minimal. You control deletion and residency; Redwood's role is advisory and to provide tooling to scrub with your KMS.
   - In both cases we integrate KMS/HSM so you can delete keys to render stored ciphertext unrecoverable (crypto-erase).

4) Proofs & audit:
   - We provide deletion receipts and an audit trail for deletion operations (who, when, scope). These are tamper-evident using signed logs.
   - SOC 2 Type II report is attached (redacted auditor cover page); we can provide a full report under an NDA.

5) Legal holds:
   - Legal holds are coordinated with our legal/security teams. For Hosted customers, we can suspend scheduled purges and export data into an audited archive; Dedicated/Private customers typically retain control and can place holds locally. We document hold requests in the audit trail.

Timelines for purge: we offer immediate soft-delete + background purge within 7 days for hosted deletions (configurable by contract). For Dedicated we will include contract language for shorter SLAs. Crypto-erase can be immediate depending on replication windows.

Next steps I propose:
 - I can share a 1-page runbook tailored to St. Mary's with exact API params, example calls for redact_strategy and deletion endpoints.
 - Evelyn (cc'd) can share a draft DPA and the SOC 2 full package under NDA.
 - If helpful, we can spin up a short Dedicated trial with retention policies set to your spec so procurement can validate.

Available for a 30 minute call tomorrow or Wednesday to lock down contract language.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas — helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions before we bring legal in: 

- You said retroactive structural redaction is limited on hosted. If we accept the hosted product but later discover PHI in logs that have been retained, what is the exact remediation path? Is there a long-form proof that the content was redacted vs. deleted?
- For the crypto-erase option: how do you handle replication windows (copies on cold storage) and can you provide an SLA for time-to-unrecoverable?
- For legal holds: does Redwood sign a clause that preserves evidence and prevents deletion until a hold is lifted (we need an auditable hold process)?

Also — procurement asked whether there is an API to request a bulk export of all records for an account (for e-discovery).

Elena — happy to take the specifics offline with legal/procurement. Quick answers so you can scope: 

- Retroactive remediation on hosted: we offer two levels — (A) deletion certificate that confirms removal of copies from active stores and indices within the purge window (7 days), and (B) an assisted archival rewrite where we remove identified PHI spans from retained artifacts (this is manual and scoped; typically available for larger agreements). We provide a signed audit entry for both operations.

- Crypto-erase SLA: standard is "key-deletion within 24 hours" on request and full irrecoverability within replication windows (up to 72 hours for cross-region replicas). We can shorten the cross-region window in contract for Dedicated customers.

- Legal hold clause: yes, we will agree to a hold-preservation clause that documents the hold request and suspends automated deletions until formal lift. The hold and any actions are recorded in the deletion audit trail.

- Bulk export API: yes — we expose an account export endpoint that streams records to a customer-owned bucket (S3/GCS/Azure). Exports are logged and signed; delivery timelines depend on data volume.

Proposed mutual action plan:
1) Sign NDA so we can send the full SOC 2 and DPA draft (DPA attached for your first pass).
2) Configure a short Dedicated trial (14 days) with retention policies set to 0/30/90 per your spec.
3) Security call with our solutions engineer next week to validate export/redaction demos.

If that works I can have our contracts lead add the DPA clause and we can route for signatures.

Thanks — Evelyn Hart
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
